quotes.text: It's called platform engineering. And here's the simplest way to think about it. This discipline creates an internal layer that absorbs complexity for developers.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: A golden path is a recommended pre-built workflow that makes the right thing the easiest thing to do.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, quotable definition of a golden path.

quotes.text: Every time a developer leaves the golden path, it tells you something real. Either the path is missing a feature it should have, or the use case genuinely doesn't belong there.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes developers leaving the paved road as valuable feedback rather than failure.

quotes.text: A platform nobody uses is just a project. It's gathering dust in a corner. Adoption is the ultimate validation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the product mindset that platform teams need.

quotes.text: AI amplifies whatever you already have. If your fundamentals are solid, like good architecture and a well-designed platform, AI makes you two to three times more productive.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why AI coding tools increase rather than replace the need for solid platforms.

chapters.title: Treating the Platform as a Product

takeaways: Shift left overloaded developers with infrastructure, security and operations work, and platform engineering puts a central layer in place to absorb that complexity.
An internal developer platform with golden paths makes the secure, tested route the easiest one, while escape hatches keep it from becoming a cage.
Run the platform as a product: talk to developers, start with one painful workflow and measure voluntary adoption instead of making it mandatory.
hook: Developers who were supposed to gain speed from DevOps now spend days on Terraform, Kubernetes and YAML instead of product code. This episode explains platform engineering, internal developer platforms and golden paths for engineering leaders and developers, and shows how to start small with one path that removes real pain.
